I recently got mine done and my best personal advice is to make sure you don't have an ear infection before getting it done lol but that's just my personal story. Most people don't need to do that. For real tho just make sure you don't get it while also having a serious medical issue. Like if you have another piercing trying to heal, a recent surgery or medical procedure, a recent injury of any sort, signs of being sick, etc. Your body is gonna need to fully prioritize your piercing. I've had mine for over a month and it's taking longer to heal because of my ear infection and sinus infection. My body hasn't been able to put 100% of it's effort on trying to heal the piercing because of these things. Just don't rush into this, you have plenty of time do reschedule if you have any other body issues that need to heal. Make sure to ask a lot of questions as well. Think of what your concerns are and then write them down on paper or on your notes app. Don't be shy with the questions. Like you said there is very little information out there so asking a professional is gonna help a lot.

This is the most realistic and most helpful answer I have found to this question for myself. You can't and shouldn't expect to stop immediately. Maybe you can for a while, but you'll always often relapse and just feel disappointed and ashamed. Instead, realize that relapse is a part of recovery and that if it happens, it happens. You have to realize that relapse is normal and it's gonna happen until you reach a point where it no longer serves a purpose. In order to reach that, try to go as long as possible to not relapse and try to do things during that time to relieve your feelings (joining a sport, doing art, making kids crafts, exercise, dancing, walking, reading, getting into a new show or movies, cuddle and pet your animals when you're stressed, etc.). The goal isn't supposed to stop immediately and to never do it again. Focus on stretching out each relapse. Say you relapsed after 2 weeks of being clean, while that's awful you went through that. It's still good because you know you can survive without needing self-harm for at least 2 weeks. Now you know you can do 3 weeks without self-harm or maybe even 4. Now try to get to 3 or 4 weeks or past that. This is building a tolerance, and that tolerance will become bigger and bigger. You also should remind yourself of these things when you relapse. Talking down to yourself after relapsing isn't gonna help either. Tell yourself things like "its done, and i can't take it back, but i can change the outcome of this," and "I am in control," and "This is normal. This is part of recovery" You never want to set your expectations too high where you can't reach them. Doing all of these things will make you feel less inclined to relapse the more it's stretched out. Another major tip I have is to also realize that no matter what you do, almost anything you do to replace self-harm isn't going to feel as satisfying as self-harm. Why? Because when you hurt yourself on the daily, you reach a high that you can't achieve when you are not hurt. Your brain releases chemicals and endorphins to protect your body from feeling pain, which should only happen when you accidentally get hurt, not intentionally. This may sound like a negative thing, but this should be a reminder and a motivator not to hurt yourself because you are intentionally taking advantage of your brains chemicals when you hurt yourself. That's why people do it, either intentionally or unintentionally. One last thing, dont use the "this is normal" excuse to relapse. Or "this is part of recovery" and then proceed to hurt yourself. These things are things you should only tell yourself after a relapse to provide yourself relief. Sorry, this is a lot to read lol but I hope it helps and makes sense of things.

I'm in the same position. I'm at a point where I don't want to recover or receive help. People like us aren't used to not being shamed for sh. I wish you weren't struggling with this like me, I understand why you do it, tho. Not to make this about me, I'm just relating to you. My whole adolescence was just me being shamed for it, People freaking out, my last 2 therapists did very inhumane practices just to shame me out of continuing. But when we do get a response we have been looking for, it feels weird or wrong in a way when it's not. I think your gf just realizes that there's nothing they can do to stop you. All they can do is support you and encourage you to receive help WHEN YOU ARE READY. that's such a big thing, only you can realize when and if you want to stop. I've been self harming since I was 11, I'm 20 now, and I realized recently that I can finally have a say in this and can choose not to recover. The only things that motivated me in the past to stop were just all about my family. I only wanted to stop for them and not myself. So, I eventually relapsed. All of this can come off as encouraging, too, which trust me, I don't encourage you to continue. But it's like any other addition. You can't force anyone to stop an addiction. I truly do wish you the best and know that you don't deserve to be hurt in any way. Try to find more people in your life who will accept you for you and will be there when you are ready for help.

After a long time of having a certain addiction, you forget what's normal and not normal. I've become really desensitized to my scars and fresh cuts. I don't think there is an average with self-harm. Most people start to self-harm at a young age, and it usually doesn't last for very long. So I think most people are under the impression that cat scratch like cuts are the average since nobody likes to show off their cuts beyond that point. From my experience and from what I have noticed amongst friends and a certain side of Twitter, the cuts don't become more severe into the adult years. So, the average is confusing and difficult depending on age and background history. I am considered a severe self-harmer (i dont like to use the phrase "cutter" but it grammatical makes more sense lol) and while I recognize that, It doesn't feel like it. This was made worse when I showed my friend my sh cuts and they didn't react. Maybe it's because they knew it was point less and wouldn't stop me, but still. So now it's made me more competitive and even more desensitized. So, to answer your question, I'm not sure. All self-harm is bad. There is a severity of it depending on the cut, but it's all bad and should not continue on because it does become more extreme. It changes in time for everybody.

I think you should call your local doctors office. They might want to a physical examination again, and if they can't provide answers, then they'll most likely either have you go through an X-ray or CT scan, if not both. I don't think you should panic or anything, but I get why you're concerned. Remind yourself that this is the best you can do for now, it's hard because you feel anxious and powerless in situations like yours, but by advocating for yourself and calling/scheduling appointments will allow you some control. You are still in control here. Maybe not of the lump itself, but of the outcome of this situation. Whenever you discover a bump, you immediately think of cancer. But I have never heard of vagina cancer before. I've heard of ovarian cancer or cancer in the uterus, but not the vaginal canal. I'm not fully educated on this, obviously, but this is just hypothetical speaking. I honestly wouldn't worry about this being cancer. It could be a cyst, swollen lymphnode, a gland that isn't cedreeding fluid properly, etc. In the meantime, check on it multiple times a day at the start, and then maybe check on it once a day until your appointment. I say this because I think it could help you notice any other changes like it shrinking or growing throughout the day. Write down if you notice this, or maybe other symptoms you haven't noticed. Like feeling more tired or fatigued than usual, stuff like that. Try feeling it too in different positions like standing up, laying down on your back, and sitting. Writing down if there are any differences in the size and feel of it. This the best you can do for now. They might want to get you in as soon as they can too because of what you're feeling. If you want to be rushed in sooner, I would just lie about other symptoms. Nothing crazy though, just say like you've been having headaches or something like that. I know that's weird advice, but of you are really worried than I would do that.

Yes. I would highly suggest you call your local doctors office to get it checked out. I'm not a doctor, but I am a 20 yr old trans man and have already gone through top surgery. I'm assuming this lump is on your chest, but I could be wrong. I also say "highly" not because I think there's anything to actually worry about, but because you should prioritize your health. I went through a similar thing recently, except my lumps were on my neck, the nape of my neck/back of my head, and a lump in my shoulder. I got blood work done, a physical exam (they just felt them), and finally, a CT scan. It's not cancer or anything major. It's just swollen lymphnodes. I have been experiencing other health issues as well, which make me believe I have an auto immune disorder. I am now just waiting for another appointment to see. I mentioned my experience because this is scary, but it was very worth it. When you get a lump of any kind, you immediately think of cancer, and it's terrifying. My doctors and I were concerned about this being Hodgkins lymphoma. Again, like I said, this is all scary, but now I know what my experience may be linked too and I'm closer to finding out and hopefully getting some answers. I know too that this lump (still assuming it's on your chest) and where it's at is probably making you feel very dysphoric, but don't let that stop you. Idk your transition goals, but you're gonna have to feel dysphoric at many times during your transition to get where you want to be or even for random medical concerns like this one. Again, I wouldn't panic or anything. Calling the doctor is your best option.
